issues.description: [suggestion] Auto-generate a weekly grocery list from the assigned diet plan. USER PROBLEM: users get a 7-day plan (DietPlanWeek) but must manually work out what to buy to actually cook it — adherence dies at the grocery store, the biggest gap between having a plan and following it. EVIDENCE: the backend already serves per-ingredient data (name + quantity + unit) for every meal (RecipeDetail consumes recipe.ingredients); DietPlanWeek already loads the whole week. A grep shows zero existing grocery/shopping code, so this is a genuine gap. Comparable trackers (Mealime, Eat This Much, PlateJoy) ship auto grocery lists as a headline retention feature. V1 SCOPE: new route /diet-plan/shopping-list reached from a 'Shopping list' button on DietPlanWeek. Client-side only, NO backend change: flatten ingredients across the week's assigned meals, sum duplicates by normalised name+unit, sort alphabetically (skip a category taxonomy in v1), render a check-off list with checked state persisted in localStorage. Add one 'Copy as text / Share' button (WhatsApp-heavy India audience) so the list can be sent to whoever shops. EFFORT: roughly 1-2 days frontend, no backend, no schema. Reuses the existing diet-plan query and ingredient shape.

issues.reviewReason: FIXED (commit fb88bd3d). Root cause: When a workout session auto-completes (all exercises done), backend sets WorkoutSessionLog.completed_at. If user taps Log Set again (e.g. on a re-opened exercise), backend returns 400 'Workout already completed.' — which showed as a red destructive toast. Fix: Activity.tsx logSetMutation.onError now detects 'already completed' pattern and shows a friendly 'Workout complete! Your session is already finished — great work.' toast instead. The sets that were logged before completion are all saved correctly (no data loss). testGate=true, no workout set tests exist. Please resolve manually.

issues.reviewReason: FIXED (commit fb88bd3d, pushed to main). Root cause: (1) NutritionMealCard used <label><Checkbox> — on Android Capacitor the label click propagated to the Radix button triggering both OS native touch haptic AND our Haptics.selectionChanged(), giving double vibration. (2) check-pop animation had scale(1.2) overshoot that looked like a flash on the pink circle. Fix: replaced label+Checkbox with a native <button> that renders the check circle directly + fires triggerHaptic('light') once in onClick. Updated check-pop keyframe to gentle scale(0.75->1) with opacity fade — no overshoot. testGate=true, no NutritionMealCard tests exist. Please resolve manually.
